prompt:
Design and implement the migration architecture for the Chicago management estate described in `fixtures/estate-inventory.json`. The destination is VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0.1.0: VMware Aria Operations, VMware Aria Automation, and VMware Aria Operations for Logs must become VCF Operations, VCF Automation, and VCF Operations for Logs while preserving every supported content/configuration item. This is an architecture deliverable, not an explanatory report.

Before implementing it, use your own network research tools to fetch real, currently reachable Broadcom-published material covering all four of these subjects: supported product migration/upgrade paths, content/configuration compatibility, end-of-general-support boundaries, and the vSAN OSA/ESA host-and-network tradeoff. Do not treat the local compatibility snapshot as a substitute for that research. Record each Broadcom source you actually consulted as an object in `research-sources.json` using `title`, `publisher`, `url` (HTTPS), `accessedOn` (YYYY-MM-DD), and `supports`. Use only these `supports` subject labels: `migration-path`, `content-compatibility`, `support-boundary`, and `storage-network`. Search terms and exact URLs are your choice. Do not add cached pages, copied search results, or a network fixture.

Use `fixtures/compatibility-snapshot.json` as the pinned implementation and grading authority where a live source has changed since the snapshot. Build `VcfMigrationArchitecture/VcfMigrationArchitecture.psd1` and `.psm1` as a PowerShell 7 module. Export `New-VcfMigrationInstallerSpec`, which accepts `-InventoryPath`, `-CompatibilityPath`, and `-OutputPath`, consumes the two supplied JSON inputs, and deterministically writes `installer-spec.json`. The harness installs `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Installer` as a prerequisite: declare that exact module dependency in the manifest and use its VCF Installer operation discovery from your module to include the `POST /v1/sddcs/validations`, `POST /v1/sddcs/resources-calculation`, and `POST /v1/sddcs` bindings, but do not vendor any VMware module or assembly.

The generated `installer-spec.json` must validate against `spec/vcf-migration-installer-spec.schema.json`. It must compare both OSA and ESA using the pinned host counts and physical network requirements, select the pinned design, name its required network changes, and place and size every target management component. Its ordered migration plan must name every inventoried source product and exact version, its target component/version and migration mode, account exactly once for every inventoried content item as carried forward or abandoned, and attach one or more concrete technical gates to every step. Include the pinned support boundary for every source product and make dependencies point only to earlier steps. Keep all paths relative to this repository and put no credentials in the outputs.

Run the module to create the checked-in `installer-spec.json`; the verifier regenerates it and requires the two objects to match. The acceptance command is `pwsh -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File tests/verify.ps1`. Do not modify anything under `fixtures/`, `spec/`, or `tests/`, and do not submit a narrative migration document.
